# Moving simplex cap groups: moment stationarity, stability, and an instability

This note enlarges the fixed-cap model by allowing the affine thresholds
of each group to move while their sum stays fixed. It derives the exact
first stationarity equations and tests both negative-Hessian examples in
multiple-simplex-cap-groups-threshold-variance-and-stability.md.

The outcome is different for the two examples. The cyclic concurrent
groups on one simplex remain strict local volume maximizers modulo
common translation. The equal-budget two-fiber example retains its
first stress but admits an actual second-order improvement once its
group thresholds can move. Neither example uses the actual critical
mixed-depth budget in a way that proves or disproves OC.

All continuous cap normal directions are fixed throughout. Moving
the group thresholds and meeting points is allowed; independently
rotating the caps about those points is not part of this model.

## 1. Affine threshold motions and the exact base moments

Fix barycentric affine functions L_i on R^d, i=0,...,d, with
sum_i L_i=1 and reference simplex T={L_i>=0}. Put m=d+1.
At a finite set P of integer bases let the reference fibers be

    K_z=c_z+r_z T,    r_z>0,    V_z=|K_z|.

The actual labeled vertex values of L_i on K_z are

    b_zi+r_z delta_ij,

where sum_i b_zi=1-r_z. This defines b_zi without treating L_i as
a linear function. In coordinates L_i(x)=l_i*x+beta_i, explicitly
b_zi=l_i*c_z+(1-r_z)beta_i.

For group g consider the fixed continuous normal directions and the
affine base thresholds

    H_gi={L_i(x)>=a_gi(z)},    a_gi(z) affine in z.

Allow a_gi to change by epsilon h_gi, where every h_gi is affine and
sum_i h_gi=0 identically. Thus sum_i a_gi(z) is preserved at every
real base. A group covers its whole continuous fiber space exactly
when sum_i a_gi(z)<=1, so its projected coverage set is preserved.
Concurrency in a given fiber is the equality case.

For a proper trace put

    t_giz=(a_gi(z)-b_zi)/r_z in (0,1),
    D_giz=d V_z (1-t_giz)^(d-1)/r_z.

Its volume is V_z(1-t_giz)^d, and differentiation gives exactly

    C_gi'=-sum_z D_giz h_gi(z).                       (1)

Strictly full and strictly empty traces contribute zero to (1);
their type persists locally. We work in this proper/full/empty open
chamber. A supporting facet with t=0 has a one-sided derivative and
cannot be silently assigned either open-chamber formula.

Let ell_gi>=0 be cap multipliers and use objective coefficient one.
Define the affine moment vector

    S_gi=sum_z D_giz (1,z) in R^(n+1).

The Lagrangian derivative with respect to ALL the allowed threshold
motions vanishes if and only if, for each group, there is a vector nu_g
such that

    ell_gi S_gi=nu_g             for every i.         (2)

Indeed one can change the affine threshold of index i by any affine
function and that of index j by its negative. This proves necessity
and sufficiency, including the constant and every base moment.
The factor 1/r_z in D is essential; probability normalization per
fiber would give the wrong equations.

When each fiber's physical vertices are also independently free,
joint stationarity combines (2) with their physical equations. For
proper traces define

    eta_giz=ell_gi(1-t_giz)^d,
    e_zi=sum_g eta_giz,
    chi_zi=sum_g eta_giz d[(1-t_giz)^(-1)-1].

If all traces are proper, the equations are exactly

    e_zi=e_z,    chi_zi=1-d e_z      for every i.     (3)

They follow from the independent off-diagonal vertex coefficients,
as in the cited threshold-variance note. With strict full traces,
replace 1 in (3) by

    w_z=1-sum_(g,i strictly full on z) ell_gi;

strict empty traces add nothing. Equations (2) and (3) are a joint
first-order test, not an assertion that a supplied stress exists or
that it has a prescribed effective support.

## 2. The one-fiber concurrent examples already pass the new first test

On one reference simplex, write a_gi for its proper normalized
thresholds and suppose sum_i a_gi=1. Equation (2) becomes

    kappa_g=ell_gi(1-a_gi)^(d-1), independent of i.   (4)

For nonnegative multipliers, joint body and threshold stationarity
is then equivalent to

    sum_g kappa_g=1/d,
    sum_g kappa_g a_gi=1/(dm)       for every i.      (5)

To check this directly, set K=sum_g kappa_g and
A_i=sum_g kappa_g a_gi. Then e_i=K-A_i and chi_i=d A_i.
Equation (3), and sum_i A_i=K, give exactly (5), and conversely.
Thus the group's meeting points must average to the simplex centroid
under the probability weights d kappa_g.

For the all-dimensional cyclic example, with

    a_gg=1-d/(3m),    a_gi=1/(3m) for i!=g,

the existing multipliers satisfy kappa_g=1/(dm). The same is true for
the planar cyclic permutations of (4/5,1/10,1/10), whose existing
high and low multipliers are 5/6 and 5/27: both products in (4)
equal 1/6. Hence moving the concurrent group points does not destroy
either example's first stationarity.

## 3. Their joint constrained Hessian is strictly negative modulo translation

The following calculation applies to any collection of proper concurrent
groups satisfying (5), with all ell_gi>0, provided the vectors a_g
affinely span the hyperplane sum a_i=1. Both cyclic examples do.

Write W=I+epsilon B and move a_gi by epsilon h_gi, where every
column sum of B and every group sum of h vanish. Put

    T=tr B,    b_i=B_ii,    s_i=sum_(j!=i)B_ij,
    v_i=T+s_i-d b_i.

Then sum_i v_i=0. The exact logarithmic derivatives of one cap are

    (log F_gi)'=v_i+d X_gi(b_i-h_gi),
    (log F_gi)''=-tr(B^2)-d X_gi^2(b_i-h_gi)^2
                            +sum_(j!=i)(b_i-B_ij)^2,          (6)

where X_gi=1/(1-a_gi). These are derivatives along a straight joint
vertex/threshold path of the exact rational cut-simplex formula.

Consider a critical velocity for all individual cap budgets, so that
every cap first derivative is zero. Formula (6) gives

    h_gi=b_i+(1-a_gi)v_i/d.

Its group sum is zero exactly when

    dT=a_g*v             for every g.               (7)

Affine spanning and sum v_i=0 force v=0, and then T=0.
Consequently h_gi=b_i for every group. There is a unique decomposition

    B=b 1^T+E,
    sum_i b_i=0,
    E_ii=0,    E 1=0,    1^T E=0.                  (8)

The first term and the threshold changes describe a common translation
of the simplex and all its group points. On (8), tr(B^2)=tr(E^2)
and sum_(i!=j)(b_i-B_ij)^2=||E||_F^2.
Moreover the first log derivatives vanish and b_i-h_gi=0.
Since e_i=1/m by (5), the exact joint Lagrangian Hessian is

    L''/V=-||E||_F^2/m.                              (9)

Thus the only critical null directions are common translations.
In particular there is no omitted positive cap-motion direction on
this critical tangent.

This proves actual strict local volume maximality modulo that symmetry.
For precision, translate any nearby joint configuration so that all
diagonal entries of W are equal: subtract from every vertex and every
group threshold the vector with entries W_ii-tr(W)/m. Its sum is zero,
and all cap masses, group sums and the objective are unchanged.
On this gauge the critical tangent has b=0, so (9) is negative definite.
Stationarity, positive multipliers and Taylor expansion then give a
local quadratic volume loss on the feasible set in this gauge.
One elementary proof takes a hypothetical feasible sequence violating
such a quadratic loss. Its normalized secants have cap derivatives
nonpositive in the limit. Since the objective derivative is their
strictly positive weighted sum, a sequence with no quadratic loss
forces every limiting cap derivative to vanish. The limiting unit
direction is critical, contradicting (9). This also treats constraints
that decrease to first order, not only paths assumed critical in advance.

No global maximality among arbitrary convex bodies is asserted.
In particular this is not local maximality in a problem that also
allows independent continuous-normal rotations.

## 4. The equal-budget two-fiber stress also passes the affine moment test

Now use the two triangles T_2 at bases z=0,1 from the variance note.
For each i=0,1,2 the two groups are

    a_Li(z)=1/10+(7/10)z,
    a_Hi(z)=4/5-(7/10)z.

All six original global budgets equal 17V/20. At base zero the L
group covers the whole plane, and at base one the H group does.
These groups need not be concurrent at those bases: their sums are
3/10+21z/10 and 12/5-21z/10. The permitted motions preserve these
two sums exactly, so this coverage persists.

All six multipliers are ell=5/11. Equation (2), divided by V, is

    nu_L=(1,2/11),    nu_H=(1,9/11),                 (10)

independently of the cap index i. Thus affine base moments do not
invalidate the given first stress. Nevertheless the extra threshold
variables change the second-order conclusion.

## 5. An exact positive critical joint velocity

Put c=(1,-1,0)^T and use the canonical positive lift

    B=[[-1,-2/5, 1/5],
       [ 2/5,1,-1/5],
       [ 3/5,-3/5,0]].

Use vertex velocities B at base zero and -B at base one. Their
traces vanish. Let the threshold velocities at these bases be the
following scalar multiples of c:

    (h_L0,h_L1,h_H0,h_H1)
            =(-1/10,83/200,-83/200,1/10) * c.       (11)

Interpolate these endpoint values affinely in z. Every group threshold
sum remains unchanged.

For one triangle and one constant threshold a, the normalized cap
first derivative in this lift is

    [(9/5)(1-a)^2-2(1-a)]c_i
                          -2(1-a)h_i.

The body coefficients are -171/500 at a=1/10 and -41/125 at a=4/5.
Inserting (11), with opposite body velocities at the two bases,
gives exactly zero for each of the six GLOBAL cap derivatives.
It also gives zero total first volume derivative.

Using the exact second formula in (6), now summing each cap over both
fibers before imposing its budget, yields

    D^2(M-(5/11)sum_gi C_gi)[delta,delta]/V
                       =3159/11000>0.              (12)

This is a rational identity, verified directly from the cut-simplex
volume formula. Imposing separate cap neutrality at both individual
fibers would be an incorrect stronger constraint and would miss (12).

## 6. An explicit acceleration and an actual strict improvement

Here is a right inverse for the six GLOBAL first cap derivatives,
normalized by V. Given a desired six-vector f_gi, set

    S_g=sum_i f_gi,
    T_0=5(9 S_L-2 S_H)/77,
    T_1=5(-2 S_L+9 S_H)/77.

Give the two triangles the additional vertex directions

    D_z=(T_z/2)(I-11^T/3).

Their contributions to each group's total first derivative are constant
over the three indices. Their group sums are

    [9/5,2/5; 2/5,9/5] (T_0,T_1)^T=(S_L,S_H)^T.

For each group put r_gi=f_gi-S_g/3, and add threshold directions only
at base zero:

    k_gi(0)=-r_gi/[2(1-a_gi(0))],    k_gi(1)=0.     (13)

They have group sum zero and are affine after interpolation. Formula
(1) shows that (D,k) has precisely the desired first cap derivative f.
Thus the construction is an explicit right inverse, not merely a
rank assertion.

Let q_gi be the normalized straight-path second derivatives of the six
caps along (11). Apply this right inverse to

    f_gi=-1/100-q_gi,

and use its output as the second acceleration in

    W_z(t)=I+t B_z+(t^2/2)D_z,
    a_gi(z,t)=a_gi(z)+t h_gi(z)+(t^2/2)k_gi(z).

All six total cap second derivatives are -V/100. By first stationarity
and (12), the total volume second derivative is

    [3159/11000-(5/11)(6/100)]V=2859 V/11000>0.

All first derivatives vanish. Analyticity gives strictly larger volume
and mass in each of the six moving caps strictly below its original
budget for all sufficiently small positive t. The companion exact verifier also
checks a concrete rational time t=1/1000.
At that time the exact normalized volume gain is

    (M(t)-2V)/V=503186538043641/3872000000000000000000>0,

and direct rational evaluation verifies all six strict budget
inequalities and all proper-cut vertex signs.

Every column of W_z(t) sums to one. Every threshold group sum stays
equal to its original affine function of z. At small t all triangles
remain nondegenerate and each cap retains its designated unique positive
vertex. The convex hull over the exposed bases 0 and 1 has exactly
these two integer fibers. Thus compatibility, integer support, the
original coverage sets and all six original budgets are simultaneously
preserved. This explicitly refutes local maximality of the equal-budget
example in the enlarged moving-threshold problem.

## 7. Limits of the conclusion

The cap derivative equation is an equality of global affine base
moments, not a separate equality in every fiber. Separate equalities
follow only when the available affine functions can isolate those
fibers, and still apply to the multiplier-weighted section factors.
Even over two independent bases, global cap budgets must not be
replaced by separate per-fiber budgets.

The one-fiber examples show that threshold variance need not disappear
when group meeting points are variables. The two-fiber example shows
that negative definiteness in physical vertex variables alone does
not establish joint stability after those variables are added.
The latter example's covering budget remains noncritical: its original
maximum mixed depth is 4V/9, while the six budgets are 17V/20.
No assertion about a general attained critical cover or an OC reduction
is made.

The standard-library verifier ../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_movable_simplex_cap_groups.py
passes 56 exact critical-Hessian checks in dimensions 2 through 8,
the affine moment identities, all six critical derivatives, the
positive joint Hessian and explicit acceleration, and the complete
rational-time actual body/cap certificate. The all-dimensional
stability statement follows from (6)-(9), not the finite checks.
